items.stem: What argument would you give for the necessity of a cell wall in plants usually fixed in one place versus in animals usually moving from one place to the other?
items.answer: Plants are rooted in one location and cannot physically move to seek shelter from harsh environmental stresses like strong winds, heavy rain, or temperature extremes. The rigid cell wall provides them with the necessary structural strength, protection, and ability to remain upright against these conditions. In contrast, animals can actively move to seek shelter or avoid danger, so they do not require a rigid outer layer, and lacking a cell wall allows their bodies the vital flexibility needed for locomotion.

items.stem: What consequences would you predict for a plant cell if its cell wall were to become as flexible as a cell membrane?
items.answer: If the plant cell wall became as flexible as a cell membrane, the plant would lose its structural rigidity and ability to stand upright, causing it to quickly wilt or collapse. Additionally, the cell would become highly vulnerable to bursting in dilute environments because it relies on the rigid cell wall to push back against the internal pressure of water entering via osmosis.
items.concept: Cell wall maintains plant cell shape

items.stem: Why is it important to cut the two potato pieces in roughly equal size and measure their initial weight before placing them in different liquids?
items.answer: Cutting the potato pieces into roughly equal sizes ensures that both pieces have a similar starting surface area, making the rate and extent of osmosis comparable between the two experimental setups. Measuring the initial weight establishes a critical baseline to accurately calculate the difference in mass after the experiment concludes. Without this initial measurement, it would be impossible to scientifically determine or quantify exactly how much water was gained or lost by the potato cells due to osmosis in the different solutions.

items.stem: Do white flowers contain any pigment? Give reasons.
items.answer: White flowers generally do not contain any specific white pigment to give them their colour. Instead, their cells contain colourless plastids called leucoplasts, which lack pigment and are primarily used for storing starch, oils, or proteins. The white appearance of the petals is actually caused by the reflection and scattering of all visible light by the microscopic air spaces and cellular structures within the flower tissue.

items.stem: Draw a well-labelled schematic diagram of a plant or an animal cell using these clues — (i) Nucleus appears as a dark and round body inside the cell. (ii) ER spreads like a network of extended nuclear envelope. (iii) Mitochondria and chloroplasts are rod shaped. You may refer to figure.
items.answer: The diagram should show the cell's outer boundary labelled cell membrane, with a cell wall drawn outside it if a plant cell is chosen. Inside the cytoplasm, the nucleus is drawn as a dark, round body enclosed by a nuclear envelope; the endoplasmic reticulum is drawn as a network of tubes and sheets spreading out from that nuclear envelope; and the mitochondria are drawn as rod-shaped bodies. A plant cell also shows rod-shaped chloroplasts and a large central vacuole. Every part drawn must carry a label.
items.reproduction_note: diagram-only answer; model answer authored from the stem's own clues

items.stem: Instead of many small ones, why does a cell not have a single giant mitochondrion? How does this relate to the concept of surface area?
items.answer: A cell has many small mitochondria rather than a single giant one to maximize the total surface area available for energy-producing chemical reactions. Mitochondria generate energy along their inner membranes, and having multiple smaller organelles significantly increases the overall surface area-to-volume ratio within the cell. This larger total surface area ensures a much faster, more efficient production and distribution of ATP to meet the continuous energy demands of the cell.

items.stem: If the skin cells start dividing by meiosis instead of mitosis, what do you think will happen to a cut on the skin?
items.answer: If skin cells divided by meiosis, the cut would not heal properly because meiosis produces daughter cells that are genetically different and contain only half the normal number of chromosomes. For damaged tissue to be repaired effectively, the new replacement cells must be exact genetic copies of the original skin cells with a full set of chromosomes, a process that can only be achieved through mitosis.

items.stem: Differentiate between the following pairs of terms based on the clues given in parentheses: (i) Cell membrane and cell wall (permeability) (ii) RER and SER (structure) (iii) Chloroplasts and chromoplasts (pigments)
items.answer: (i) Cell membrane and cell wall (permeability) : The cell membrane is selectively permeable, meaning it allows only certain substances to pass through while blocking others. In contrast, the plant cell wall is freely permeable, allowing water and dissolved minerals to pass through it without strict selectivity. (ii) RER and SER (structure) : Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) appears rough under an electron microscope because it has tiny structures called ribosomes attached to its surface. Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) appears smooth because it lacks these attached ribosomes on its surface. (iii) Chloroplasts and chromoplasts (pigments): Chloroplasts contain the green pigment chlorophyll, which is essential for trapping sunlight during photosynthesis. Chromoplasts contain other colored pigments, such as yellow, orange, or red, which impart bright colors to flower petals and fruits to attract pollinators and animals.

items.stem: Two similar animal cells are placed in two different solutions: • Cell X is placed in pure water. • Cell Y is placed in a concentrated salt solution. Cells are observed after some time. Cell X swells, and Cell Y shrinks. Which statement provides the correct explanation for the above observations? (i) Salt molecules moved into Cell Y, causing it to shrink. (ii) Water moved into Cell X and more water moved out of Cell Y than the salt solution entered in it. (iii) Water moved into Cell X and moved out of Cell Y through the cell membrane. (iv) Solute movement caused osmosis in both cells.
items.answer: Option (iii) Water moved into Cell X and moved out of Cell Y through the cell membrane. Justification: Osmosis is the movement of water across a selectively permeable membrane. Pure water is a dilute medium causing water to enter and swell Cell X, while the concentrated salt solution draws water out of Cell Y, causing it to shrink.

items.stem: Look at the diagram of a cell in figure. Identify the parts labelled from (a) to (g) and correctly match them with their functions given below: (i) Controlling all the activities of a cell. (ii) Site of cellular respiration. (iii) Storage organelle that also provides rigidity to the cell. (iv) Separates the cell contents from surroundings. (v) Provides structural rigidity to the cell. (vi) Packs and stores materials received from ER. (vii)Helps in manufacturing food.
items.answer: Based on Figure showing a plant cell, the parts and their matched functions are: (a) Nucleus: (i) Controlling all the activities of a cell. (b) Golgi apparatus: (vi) Packs and stores materials received from ER. (c) Chloroplast: (vii) Helps in manufacturing food. (d) Cell wall: (v) Provides structural rigidity to the cell. (e) Cell membrane: (iv) Separates the cell contents from surroundings. (f) Mitochondria: (ii) Site of cellular respiration. (g) Vacuole: (iii) Storage organelle that also provides rigidity to the cell.

items.stem: Which of the following option(s) of the pairs of cell organelles are correctly placed under the given categories? Each option gives one organelle Present in the plant cells and one organelle Absent in the animal cells: (i) Leucoplast / Cell wall (ii) Mitochondria / Ribosome (iii) Cell wall / Golgi apparatus (iv) Lysosome / Endoplasmic reticulum
items.answer: Option (i) is correctly placed. Leucoplasts are plastids found in plant cells for storage, and the cell wall is an outer rigid structure present in plant cells but completely absent in animal cells. The other options list organelles like ribosomes, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum as absent in animal cells, which is factually incorrect as animal cells possess all of these.
items.concept: Absence of cell wall in animals

items.stem: Two students, Renu and Rohit, were having a discussion on the plastids. Renu emphasised that all parts of the plants, even roots, contain plastids. However, Rohit did not agree with the statement and told her that plastids are absent in plant roots since the roots are underground and do not need to perform photosynthesis. Who is correct? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Renu is correct. While Rohit is right that underground roots generally do not perform photosynthesis, plastids serve more functions than just capturing sunlight. Plant roots contain a type of colourless plastid called leucoplasts. These leucoplasts do not have pigments but play a crucial role in storing food materials such as starch, oils, or proteins for the plant, proving that plastids are indeed present in roots.

items.stem: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are two important organelles in a plant cell. Discuss how these two organelles are structurally and functionally similar to each other, and different from each other.
items.answer: Structurally, both mitochondria and chloroplasts are similar because they are double-membrane-bound organelles and both contain their own DNA and ribosomes, allowing them to synthesise some of their own proteins. Functionally, they are similar in that both are deeply involved in cellular energy processes. However, they differ significantly in their specific roles. Mitochondria are the powerhouses of the cell that carry out cellular respiration to break down food and release energy in the form of ATP. In contrast, chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the sites of photosynthesis, where they capture light energy to synthesise food (sugars) for the plant cell.

items.stem: Which of the following pairs of cell organelles contains DNA? (i) Chloroplasts, Ribosomes (ii) Mitochondria, Nucleus (iii) Golgi bodies, Ribosomes (iv) Nucleus, Lysosomes
items.answer: Option (ii) Mitochondria, Nucleus. Justification: The nucleus holds the chromatin, a set of coded instructions containing the primary genetic material (DNA) of the cell. Additionally, mitochondria are unique organelles that possess their own circular DNA, sharing this trait with plastids like chloroplasts.

items.stem: A researcher carried out an experiment in which she took two carrots of similar size. She placed one carrot in plain water and the other carrot in concentrated salt solution. After 24 hours she recorded her observations. (i) What hypothesis does she want to test through this experiment? (ii) What would you suggest for the improvement of this experiment? (iii) Why does the carrot in plain water stay stiff and crunchy, but the carrot in concentrated salt solution become rubbery and limp?
items.answer: (i) The researcher likely wants to test the hypothesis that plant cells will undergo osmosis depending on their surrounding medium, specifically that they will absorb water in a dilute solution and lose water in a concentrated solute solution. (ii) To improve the experiment, the researcher should measure and record the initial weight and precise dimensions of both carrots before placing them in the solutions. By comparing these initial measurements with the final weight and dimensions after 24 hours, she would obtain reliable quantitative data to support her visual observations. (iii) The carrot in plain water stays stiff because plain water is a dilute solution, causing water to enter the carrot cells via osmosis and build up firm turgor pressure against the cell walls. The carrot in the concentrated salt solution becomes rubbery because the surrounding solution has a lower water concentration, causing water to move out of the carrot cells into the solution, leading to a loss of internal pressure and firmness.

items.stem: Indicate the presence or absence of the following structures in bacterial and animal cells: chromosome, nucleus, mitochondria, Golgi complex, chromoplasts.
items.answer: Chromosome - bacterial cell: present; animal cell: present. Nucleus - bacterial cell: absent; animal cell: present. Mitochondria - bacterial cell: absent; animal cell: present. Golgi complex - bacterial cell: absent; animal cell: present. Chromoplasts - bacterial cell: absent; animal cell: absent.

items.stem: Carry out the following experiment: Take four peeled potato halves and scoop each one out to make potato cups. One of these potato cups should be made from a boiled potato. Place each of the potato cups in a beaker containing water. Now, set up the experiment as follows: (a) Keep Cup A empty. (b) Add one teaspoon sugar in Cup B. (c) Add one teaspoon salt in Cup C. (d) Add one teaspoon sugar in the boiled potato in Cup D. Observe the four potato cups at least two hours and answer the following questions: (i) Explain why water gathers in the hollowed portion of Cup B and Cup C. (ii) Why is Cup A necessary for this experiment? (iii) Explain why water does not gather in the hollowed portions of Cups A and D.
items.answer: (i) Water gathers in Cup B and Cup C due to the process of osmosis. The addition of sugar and salt creates a highly concentrated solution inside the potato cups. Because the living potato cells act as a selectively permeable membrane, water moves from the area of higher water concentration in the beaker into the hollowed cups to balance the solute concentrations. (ii) Cup A acts as a control for the experiment. By remaining empty and showing that water does not gather inside on its own, it proves that the movement of water into Cups B and C is specifically caused by the presence of the solutes (sugar and salt). (iii) Water does not gather in Cup A because there is no solute inside to create a concentration gradient that would draw water in. Water does not gather in Cup D because boiling the potato kills its cells and destroys the selectively permeable nature of the cell membranes, which is an absolute requirement for osmosis to take place.

items.stem: Identify the pair that incorrectly matches the cell organelle with its function. (i) Ribosome — Protein synthesis (ii) SER — Lipid and cellulose synthesis (iii) Lysosome — Digestion of foreign agents
items.answer: Option (ii) SER — Lipid and cellulose synthesis is the incorrectly matched pair. While the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) is indeed involved in the synthesis and storage of fats and lipids, it does not synthesise cellulose. Cellulose is a carbohydrate primarily found in the plant cell wall, and its synthesis is not a function of the SER.

items.stem: What outcome do you expect, if all the mitochondria are removed from a eukaryotic cell?
items.answer: If all mitochondria are removed from a eukaryotic cell, the cell will lose its ability to perform cellular respiration and generate energy. Because mitochondria act as the powerhouses that supply ATP for most cellular activities, the sudden lack of energy would quickly cause vital cell functions to stop, ultimately leading to the death of the cell.

items.stem: Which phenomenon inhibits the formation of tumors in the human body? Can plants also develop tumors? Explain.
items.answer: The phenomenon that inhibits the formation of tumors in the human body is called contact inhibition, a process where normal cells stop dividing uncontrollably when they come in contact with neighbouring cells. Plants can also develop tumors, but they do so differently. Because plant cells have rigid cell walls, they do not exhibit contact inhibition like animal cells do, meaning their cells follow a different pattern of growth and can still form tumor-like growths when control systems fail.

items.stem: The cell membrane of a cell is made up of proteins and lipids. Which cell organelles help in the synthesis of cell membrane? Write the path of these compounds from their site of synthesis to the cell membrane and show this through a labelled diagram.
items.answer: The Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) and the Golgi apparatus help in the synthesis of the cell membrane. The Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER) synthesises the membrane proteins, and the Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) synthesises the membrane lipids. Once produced, these proteins and lipids travel in transport vesicles from the ER to the Golgi apparatus. The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages these materials into new secretory vesicles, which then move to and fuse with the existing cell membrane, expanding it.

items.stem: What would happen if gametes are formed by mitotic divisions?
items.answer: If gametes were formed by mitosis instead of meiosis, they would contain a full set of chromosomes identical to the parent cell, rather than having half the number. When these gametes combined during fertilisation, the resulting offspring would have double the normal number of chromosomes. This doubling would continue uncontrollably with every successive generation, destroying genetic stability and causing severe developmental failures.

items.stem: A farmer, Deepa, was very happy with the harvest of amla (Indian Gooseberry) and lemons on her farm. However, she could sell only one-fourth of the produce in the local market. Recognising that a significant amount of produce may be lost post-harvest, she employed a traditional yet scientifically sound method to extend the shelf life of amla and lemons. She turned perishable produce into profitable products, such as pickles and sharbat. She used the excess produce to prepare pickles, murabbas, and sharbat by adding appropriate amounts of salt, sugar, or jaggery to small pieces of fruit and their juices. These were then stored in small glass bottles for sale, helping her prevent the wastage of post-harvest produce. This shift from farming to agro-processing would strengthen food security and boost the local economy, creating a sustainable model that cuts waste while increasing her income. Based on the above passage answer the following questions: (i) Which scientific concept has the farmer applied in the preservation of the farm produce? (ii) How does the addition of high concentrations of salt and sugar create an environment that prevents the growth of spoilage-causing bacteria and fungi? (iii) Suggest a healthy recipe of this kind for food preservation. (iv) What are the scientific values addressed in this case?
items.answer: (i) The farmer has primarily applied the scientific concept of osmosis in preserving her farm produce. (ii) Adding high concentrations of salt or sugar creates a highly concentrated (hypertonic) environment around the food. Due to osmosis, water is drawn out of any spoilage-causing bacteria or fungi that land on the food. This severe water loss shrinks and kills the microbial cells, thereby preventing them from growing and spoiling the food. (iii) A healthy preservation recipe would be making a mixed vegetable pickle. You can cut vegetables like carrots, cauliflower, and green chilies, dry them slightly in the sun to remove surface moisture, and mix them with spices, highly concentrated salt, and a small amount of mustard oil to create an environment where spoilage microbes cannot survive. (iv) The scientific values addressed include critical thinking and problem-solving by using the biological principle of osmosis to address real-world challenges. It also demonstrates an understanding of sustainability by minimizing food waste, and shows economic awareness by applying scientific knowledge to transform perishable farm yields into long-lasting, valuable goods.
